name: Base/Radix Conversion (including unknown-radix equations)
recognitionClueHinglish: Poocha hai ek number ko ek base se doosre me convert karo, ya ek equation di hai jisme base(s) UNKNOWN hai aur solve karna hai — is topic ka sabse bada pattern hai (57 me se 18 PYQs).
whatShouldComeToMind: Positional value formula: Σ digit×base^position — apply directly for conversion.
For unknown-base equations: set up the polynomial equation, solve algebraically, remember the base must exceed every digit used in that representation.
generalSolvingApproach: 1. For direct conversion: convert to decimal first (using the positional formula) as an intermediate step, then convert decimal to the target base if needed.
2. For unknown-radix equations: write out the positional-value expressions for both sides symbolically, set equal, solve the resulting polynomial/equation for the unknown base(s).
3. Always check solution validity: the base must be a positive integer STRICTLY GREATER than the largest digit appearing in that number's representation.
variationsObserved: Multiple valid (base) solutions to count, not just find one.
Cross-base equality checks (is X in base-p equal to Y in base-q) — convert both to decimal and compare.
commonTraps: Forgetting the base-must-exceed-largest-digit validity constraint, potentially missing/including invalid solutions.
Arithmetic slips in the positional-value expansion for larger numbers — write out each term explicitly rather than doing it mentally.

name: Two's Complement Representation & Range
recognitionClueHinglish: Poocha hai ek number ki 2's complement representation kya hai, ya given bit-pattern ka decimal value kya hai, ya n-bit representation ka RANGE kya hai — is topic ka doosra bada pattern hai (57 me se 16 PYQs).
whatShouldComeToMind: To find 2's complement of a negative decimal: represent |x| in binary, invert all bits, add 1.
To find decimal value of a 2's complement bit pattern: if sign bit is 0, direct positional value; if sign bit is 1, compute -(2^n - value) or invert+add1 then negate.
generalSolvingApproach: 1. For encoding a negative number: binary of magnitude → invert all bits → add 1.
2. For decoding: check sign bit; if negative, apply the inverse procedure (subtract 1, invert, negate) or use the 2^n - value shortcut.
3. For range/bit-width questions: apply the exact asymmetric formula directly, don't assume symmetric range.
variationsObserved: Hexadecimal 2's complement representation (combine base-conversion with 2's complement encoding).
Product of two 2's complement numbers — needs up to 2n bits to represent without overflow.
Bit-width EXTENSION questions (sign-extend a smaller representation to more bits).
commonTraps: Off-by-one on the boundary of the asymmetric range.
Padding with 0s instead of sign-extending for negative number bit-width extension.
edgeCases: The most negative value (-2^(n-1)) has NO positive counterpart in the same bit width — special case worth remembering.

name: Overflow Detection in Arithmetic
recognitionClueHinglish: Do numbers add/subtract ho rahe hain (2's complement ya sign-magnitude), aur poocha hai OVERFLOW hoga ya nahi — is topic ka teesra bada pattern hai (57 me se 13 PYQs).
whatShouldComeToMind: Opposite-sign addition CANNOT overflow — only same-sign addition can.
For subtraction: convert to addition of the negation (A-B = A+(-B)), then apply the same addition-overflow rule.
generalSolvingApproach: 1. If the operands have OPPOSITE signs (for addition) — immediately conclude NO overflow possible.
2. If SAME signs: perform the actual binary addition, track the carry INTO the sign-bit position and the carry OUT of it, compare.
3. For subtraction, first negate the subtrahend (2's complement), then apply the same addition-overflow analysis.
variationsObserved: Sign-magnitude specific overflow rules (different from 2's complement's carry-based rule — sign-magnitude addition of same-sign operands overflows if the magnitude-sum exceeds the representable range directly).
Hardware-flag questions (carry flag vs overflow flag distinction in a processor's status word).
commonTraps: Confusing 'carry out of the MSB' alone with overflow — must compare carry-IN vs carry-OUT specifically at the sign bit.
Applying the 2's complement overflow rule to a sign-magnitude problem (different rules apply).

name: Bit-Counting / Special Numeric Properties (incl. floating point)
recognitionClueHinglish: Poocha hai binary representation me kitne 1's hain, ya sign-extension kya karta hai, ya zero ki kitni representations hain, ya floating-point precision/rounding related question — ye miscellaneous numeric-properties pattern hai.
whatShouldComeToMind: Count 1-bits directly by converting to binary and counting.
Sign-magnitude/1's complement have TWO zero representations (+0, -0); two's complement has ONE.
Floating point precision loss: adding a very small number to a very large one can lose the small value entirely due to limited mantissa bits (rounding).
generalSolvingApproach: 1. For bit-counting: convert to binary explicitly, count directly.
2. For zero-representation questions: recall the specific count per encoding scheme (2 for sign-magnitude/1's-complement, 1 for 2's complement).
3. For floating-point questions: consider mantissa precision limits — small differences can vanish when added to much larger magnitude numbers (catastrophic cancellation / precision loss).
variationsObserved: Storage-space reduction percentage questions (comparing character-encoded vs integer-encoded storage for numeric attributes).
Probability questions about matching bit-patterns of randomly chosen numbers (combine with basic probability).
commonTraps: Assuming floating-point arithmetic is exact/associative — order of operations can change results due to rounding at each step.
